cells.tense: You're here with it now — the fire's lit, your hand is on what feeds it, and you know why you're tending it.
cells.ask: Offer the next stretch of this — say yes to the idea that just showed up, the one you haven't tried yet. See what it feeds.
cells.core: You've built something that keeps itself going, and you're in the middle of it with your sleeves rolled up. Not pushing — knowing when to add and when to let it burn on its own. People catch their own momentum just from standing near you, and you can feel that happening. It doesn't cost you the way it used to, and you're not white-knuckling any of it.\n\nWhat you've already come through is what makes the next thing possible. Nothing in you is owed to the past anymore — it's all fuel now. So when something wants to be dreamt that you haven't earned the right to yet, you're allowed to say yes to it. You've paid for it. Say yes and watch what the wanting stirs up.
cells.sheetLine: You're tending something that keeps going because you tend it — not because you push it.
cells.verb: Tending the fire that keeps you going — feeding what's alive, holding steady, keeping it lit.
cells.place: Where what you are comes through whole, with nothing dimmed down.

cells.tense: You're out ahead of yourself, already living in a version of this that hasn't arrived — arranging everything so it will have been fine.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're holding and write down what's actually true about it today. Let the truth do the steadying.
cells.core: You keep the fire going, and it's real — people move because you haven't let it go out, and you do that with care, not force. On a good day this looks like a steady hand on the room, everyone breathing easier because someone is tending. You're not managing them. You're just keeping it warm.\n\nBut somewhere in the last stretch, tending turned into guarding — placing people, managing outcomes, making sure it all lands before anything has actually happened. You're spending tomorrow's fuel on a version of the day that isn't here. The honest look — at what's really true, at what you actually know — is what puts your feet back under you. Not less care. Just less guessing.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping it alive, and you're also outrunning it.
cells.verb: Tending the fire that keeps you going — feeding what's alive, holding steady, keeping it lit.

cells.tense: The fire's gone quiet and you're standing at a door that shut behind you, still holding the handle.
cells.ask: End one thing that's already finished. Let it go fully, and tend what's still actually alive.
cells.core: You know how to keep something going — you've done it before, with warmth, without burning out. On a good day this looks like a table where people come back because the thing you built is still warm, still theirs to sit at. That way of holding things is still in you.\n\nRight now the tending has nowhere to land. There's something you've been keeping warm that's already gone, and the keeping is what's using you up. What wants to move on is asking you to let it — not out of defeat, but because the next living thing needs the room. Release what's done and the way you keep things going comes back, pointed at something that answers.
cells.sheetLine: You've been keeping warm something that already ended.

cells.tense: You're already doing this — the way you hold people steady, the way you keep things going — you just describe it like it's happening to you.
cells.ask: Pick one place where you're the one holding it together and say, in your own words, that it's you doing it.
cells.core: Someone in the room keeps the fire lit. On a good day this looks like a kitchen where everyone ends up, because you make it easy to keep going — a warm place, a steady place, and you're the one who made it that way.\n\nYou call it circumstance — busy, just how things shook out, someone had to. But the warmth has your shape all through it. Building something real out of a clear-eyed look at what's here doesn't need a report from somewhere else. It needs you saying it's yours. Naming one thing — out loud, once — doesn't exaggerate anything. It just stops hiding it.
